proposal.hypothesis: Staging each source tile's x, y, z, and mass once in shared memory lets the active target threads in a block reuse those values, potentially reducing repeated global source loads. The interaction order and arithmetic are retained; synchronization and staging overhead may offset any benefit, so the official geometric-mean timing must decide.

retained: Stage source x, y, z, and mass into four dynamic shared-memory arrays, one source per lane per tile.
Process tiles in ascending source-index order, with unconditional block barriers around tile consumption and valid-count handling for partial tiles.
Set dynamic shared memory to 4096 bytes for the configured 256-thread block; preserve the baseline force and integration arithmetic.
